1.why: UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case, no italics or all-caps, and avoid dense text blocks.

3.why: Layout is single-column, spacious, and readable at mobile width with clear form fields.

4.why: Copy is consistently short and plain, e.g. 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.'

5.why: Verification code field shows placeholder example 'Example: 123456'.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block of text to proceed; messages stay brief.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control is shown for any codes; user must type the verification code.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears in any screenshot.

9.why: Standard email/password fields and a simple code input support browser autofill and password managers.

10.why: Step indicator and prominent blue primary buttons make the current step and main action clear.

11.why: Primary action is generally one per screen, but code-entry views show multiple actions (Send code, Check code, Send a new code).

12.why: Banners plainly confirm outcomes, e.g. 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

13.why: 'Send a new code' lets the user re-request without penalty; code field can be edited to retry.

14.why: Error states the problem and fix without blame: 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.'

15.why: Messages say 'Enter it when you are ready' with no visible countdown or reading time limit.
